title: Wave-Particle Duality in Quantum Systems
text:
Quantum physics postulates that matter exhibits both particle and wave properties, a phenomenon known as wave-particle duality. This suggests that entities like photons and electrons are not strictly confined to one mode of existence but possess characteristics of both types simultaneously.

The concept of superposition describes a quantum system existing in multiple possible states at once until it interacts with an environment or is measured. Upon observation, the system instantaneously collapses into a single definite state, illustrating the critical role that measurement plays in defining physical reality at this scale.

Understanding these principles requires a departure from classical intuition regarding determinism and locality.
